title: Bobby Pulido Wins Third Latin Grammy Days After Winning Congress Seat — and Says He's Retiring From Music
excerpt: Tejano star Bobby Pulido won Best Tejano Album at the Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday, Nov. 12, just nine days after flipping Texas' 15th Congressional District — and used his acceptance speech to announce his retirement from music.
content:
Tejano star Bobby Pulido won his third Latin Grammy on Thursday, Nov. 12, just nine days after winning a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives, and used his acceptance speech to announce his retirement from music.

Pulido took home Best Tejano Album at the 27th Annual Latin Grammy Awards in Las Vegas for Bobby Pulido & Friends: Una Tuya y Una Mía (Vol. 2/En Vivo), a live album recorded during concerts in Monterrey, Mexico, in December 2024 and released in 2025.

It was his third career Latin Grammy and his second straight win in the category, after winning in 2025 for the first volume of the live collaboration series.

On Nov. 3, the 53-year-old Edinburg native defeated incumbent Republican Rep. Monica De La Cruz in Texas' 15th Congressional District, flipping the seat to the Democrats.

"I want to tell you that I am retiring from music, and I leave this chapter filled with gratitude and so much love," Pulido said in his acceptance speech. He added that Tejano music "is in very good hands."

Pulido is set to take office in January 2027.
